current.text: He is 36 years old and is coming back from a torn Achilles.
He missed almost all of last season. Lillard, Morant and Scoot Henderson played about 15 games combined.
The Blazers reportedly plan to start Lillard and Morant together. The projected starting five is Lillard, Morant, Camara, Avdija and Clingan.

He is expected to play about 30 to 31 minutes as a low-minute starter. Portland should stagger him with Morant but close games with both. Josh rejects takes that he is washed or will play only about 25 minutes.
Portland's guard group is crowded. Morant, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson and Deni Avdija share the ball and the playmaking with him.
Morant's arrival lowers his value. Portland has too many high-usage guards for all of them to keep last season's numbers.
Minutes and usage are expected to swing from game to game across the Portland rotation.
Portland has a new head coach this season.
Teammates who finish poorly (Camara, Clingan, Avdija) are expected to turn fewer of the Portland guards' passes into assists.
The experts like his per game value. Josh took him in round 7 and thinks he could be a top 50 player per game. Another expert expects him to beat his ADP per game.

The experts also see a lot of risk. One puts him in point guard tier 7 because of his age, the Achilles, possible compensation injuries and missed time. Others call him risky because of his age and the crowded guard group, and one would not pair him with Kyrie and Davis.
In an auction mock he may have been the last player left with about 20 USD of per game value, but Josh still passed on him.
The Blazers have three back-to-backs in the fantasy playoffs.
The experts differ on back-to-backs. The team preview does not expect Portland to sit him in them, but another expert worries about back-to-backs early in the season.

durable.text: He is a very good shooter when he plays off the ball.
FT% is his best category. He shoots about 92% on solid volume, so he clearly lifts a team's FT%.
His FG% is low for a guard on high shot volume, so he hurts a team's FG%.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both rank him around 67 to 70 with an average cost near 5 USD, but Yahoo values him at 16 USD and an expert puts his per game value near 20 USD. That makes him a cheap mid-draft target if you can handle the injury and age risk. He fits punt FG% builds best, adding elite FT% (about 92%) plus good threes and assists. Early in the season, check that he plays 30 or more minutes next to Morant and whether Portland sits him on back-to-backs, since the Blazers have three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks.
